_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-05 · SkyWalker — we can now answer a training partner's "which of our occupations already earn college credit, and where?" in one pass.
_status: Ashley brought a list of 160 occupations from an employment training center and asked which ones map to CPL and which colleges honor them. 139 unique occupations went through: 51 have a statewide credit recommendation, 53 have CPL at specific colleges only, and 35 have no CPL anywhere in California. Two things came out of it that matter beyond this one partner. First, utility line work is a complete blank — lineworker, substation electrician, hydro plant, gas control, metering, cable splicer, power dispatcher, about 20 job titles, have zero CPL in the entire system. Second, the college in the partner's own county (San Joaquin Delta) has 69 CPL credentials and exactly one of them is career/technical — the other 68 are AP and CLEP exams. Modesto Junior College, 40 minutes away, has 265. A referral plan built on the nearest college would have quietly sent students to the wrong place. The tool that produced all this is now reusable: point it at any partner's occupation list and it does the same job, and each run adds to a shared crosswalk so the next partner is cheaper.

items.text: 🔁 RUN IT AGAIN, on someone else's list. The crosswalk engine has been through exactly one partner (SJCOE). The whole promise is that each partner makes the next one cheaper — that's a design intention until a second list proves it. Any workforce board, AJCC, county office or apprenticeship sponsor will do. The run tells you what it couldn't match; that list is the work.

⚡ THE BIGGEST GAP WE'VE FOUND FROM A PARTNER LIST: utility line work has ZERO CPL anywhere in the system. Lineworker, lineman, substation electrician, hydro plant operator and mechanic, gas control, metering, cable splicer, power dispatcher — about 20 job titles, nothing to offer any of them. These are IBEW and PG&E-pipeline careers with formal apprenticeships, which is normally the easiest kind of CPL to build. Worth a conversation about whether we go after it.

🏫 A college can look active on CPL and have nothing a working adult can use. San Joaquin Delta has 69 CPL credentials — 68 are AP and CLEP exams and exactly ONE is career/technical. Sacramento City and Folsom Lake have zero career credentials; Cosumnes River has none at all. Modesto Junior has 265, the most in the state. Our dashboards count credentials, not what KIND — so this is invisible today unless you go looking.

🧭 YOUR CALL — the COBI tab you green-lit. I'd build the 'what does each college actually offer CPL for, academic exams vs career/technical' view, because that's straight from the data. I would NOT publish the occupation-to-credential matching as a live tab: that part is my subject-matter judgment, and a tab makes it look more official than it is. The fix for that is a real occupation crosswalk (O*NET) — worth scoping if you want this to go public rather than hand-delivered.

📇 MAP USERS — 6 colleges need your eye. Siskiyous, Cosumnes River, Feather River, Hartnell, NOCE and Calbright have no CPL contact in MAP, so I looked up the counseling inbox each college publishes on its own website. Those are a starting point, not a MAP designation — the tab shows the source link next to each one. Gavilan needed a human to get right, so at least one of these six probably does too. Tell me the correct person and I'll record it with your name on it.

⚠ THE HEADLINE: 25 of 123 colleges have no Primary Contact email — the address MAP sends student CPL requests to. 24 of them have a live landing page, so a student asking those colleges today reaches nobody. Open MAP Users → '⚠ No student contact' (needs sign-in). 17 have a proposed person drawn from their own MAP designations; the tab drafts the email telling the college who we routed them to.

🙋 8 colleges have nobody to propose. 5 have only a VPAA or CEO on file — I deliberately did NOT route student requests to a vice president, since that's the college's call. 3 (Calbright Credit, North Orange Continuing Ed Credit, San Diego CCE Credit) have zero MAP users at all — that's the same standalone continuing-ed onboarding gap the Noncredit tab flagged, not a contact problem.

Build Jessica's cut as a live tab filter: the 71 colleges with no CPL Assistant, with the best fallback user (Primary Contact first, then the cascade). It was delivered as a chat table, which goes stale against the monthly sync. The lens plumbing already exists — it's a sibling of the gap lens.

🔗 Still open since Session 87: the exact MAP URL you want the 'update your contacts' link to point at. The draft emails currently link each college's MAP CPL dashboard. One-line change once you send it.

❓ 6 items are waiting on you (filter: 'Needs Input'). The one that unlocks the most: HOW MANY colleges and high-school partners are on the incumbent articulation system? It sizes the largest-volume lane in the whole analysis and nothing in our repos carries it. Also open: is MAP's high-school role decided or aspirational, landing-page build dates, the CDCR back-catalog, Calbright's FTES (needs Malone), and where the '44 non-CCC dental programs' figure came from.

⭐ THE BIG FINDING: 49 statewide exhibits are published across 252 college-slots with ZERO students served — only 30 of 84 statewide exhibits have ever converted a single unit. CompTIA Linux+ is live at 16 colleges and has never produced an award. The faculty work is DONE on all of these; what's missing is outreach. Cheapest volume available anywhere in CPL. The list is live in the tab and refreshes itself.

⚠ NOCE, San Diego College of Continuing Education, Mt. SAC Noncredit and Calbright appear on ZERO of MAP's 1,987 credential titles — while ~48 entries already name a specific high school. The gap isn't permission or capability; nobody has done the data entry. Highest value-for-effort item in the whole workstream.
